rounds.text: Systematic Industries Ltd is significantly undervalued by the market, trading at an attractive EV/EBITDA of 7.24x compared to the sector benchmark of 12.12x [E11]. The core operational engine is exceptionally robust, highlighted by a strong 5-year compounded profit growth of 49% and consistent 3-year profit growth matching the same high rate [E17, E18]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow valuation sets intrinsic value at Rs 411 per share, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 41.6% against the current market price of Rs 240 [E38, E39]. The reverse DCF indicates that today's price only implies a conservative 10.6% earnings growth, well below the 18.0% assumed in the base case [E40]. Capital allocation and returns also outpace the broader environment, with a solid ROCE of 16.07% outperforming the sector benchmark of 12.96% [E10]. Conceded: [E28, E32, E46].

The company carries severe underlying risks in its cash generation and working capital management, highlighted by a poor cash conversion ratio of 0.29x where reported profits vastly outpace actual operating cash flow [E28]. This disconnect is compounded by a ballooning in working capital requirements, with working capital days surging from 51.4 days to 88.9 days [E49]. Furthermore, borrowings have escalated sharply to Rs 64 Cr in Sep 2026, up dramatically from just Rs 10 Cr a year earlier [E32], while filed statements explicitly flag that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E48]. Institutional confidence is actively eroding as evidenced by negative money flow signals [E37], with foreign institutions slashing their stake from 2.55% to 0.76% and domestic institutions cutting theirs from 11.39% to 6.12% over the same period [E35, E36]. These structural financial strains are accompanied by a complete absence of shareholder returns through dividends [E4] alongside inconsistent operating margins [E26, E27]. Conceded: [E38] (the discounted cash flow model suggests a higher intrinsic value and margin of safety).

While the bear highlights a low cash conversion ratio of 0.29x for Mar 2026 [E28], the business still successfully generated positive operating cash flow of Rs 6 Cr alongside positive free cash flow of Rs 1 Cr in that period [E29, E30]. Conceded: working capital days have increased to 88.9 days [E49] and borrowings have risen to Rs 64 Cr [E32], but this coincides with a 100% expansion in capital work-in-progress to Rs 4 Cr [E33] as part of an active growth spend backed by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.30x [E31] and an overall positive assessment of debt reduction [E44]. The institutional outflow cited [E35, E36, E37] overlooks the broader macroeconomic reality that the Capital Goods sector sits firmly in a tailwind with a score of +0.58 [E56, E58], supporting strong fundamental momentum including 24% TTM sales growth [E16] and 49% compounded profit growth over 3 years [E18]. Conceded: the company does not pay out a dividend [E4, E46] and operating margins are noted as inconsistent [E26, E27], yet the rules-based screen still awards a solid 70/100 score [E50] driven by accelerating quarterly performance like net profit up 18% YoY [E52, E57].

Conceded: the company generated positive operating cash flow of Rs 6 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 1 Cr in Mar 2026 [E29, E30], and sits at a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.30x [E31]. However, this cash generation is severely undermined by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.29x, indicating that reported profits are far ahead of actual cash collected due to swelling receivables and accruals [E28]. Furthermore, the bull's defense of rising borrowings to Rs 64 Cr as mere growth spend [E32, E33] ignores the explicit flag that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E48], alongside a sharp deterioration in working capital days from 51.4 to 88.9 days [E49]. While the Capital Goods sector carries a tailwind score of +0.58 [E56, E58], this macro backdrop does not offset heavy institutional abandonment, evidenced by foreign institutions slashing holdings to 0.76% and domestic institutions dropping to 6.12% [E35, E36].
